structured_data.title: Marriage Story
structured_data.description: MARRIAGE STORY is Academy Award nominated filmmaker Noah Baumbach's incisive and compassionate look at a marriage breaking up and a family staying together. The film stars Scarlett Johansson and Adam Driver. Laura Dern, Alan Alda, and Ray Liotta co-star.

community_snippets.snippet: [Letterboxd Review of "Marriage Story"] "Marriage is the most old-fashioned way to commit suicide."A could-have-been iconoclastic classic, trapped in entirely the wrong approach. It’s a dramedy about two ordinary, middle-class, city-dwelling newlyweds, mostly in the form of vignettes on their married life together. Shim Hye-jin and Choi Min-soo are both very good as the central couple; Shim in particular, for whom this was deservedly her breakout. community_snippets.snippet: [Letterboxd Review of "Marriage Story"] Marriage Story was one of the biggest popular hits in Korea in early 90s, which popularized Shim Hye-jin's career in the 90s, who would grow to be one of the most awarded actresses in the country during the decade, and also helped popularize Choi Min-soo's career, who used to be one of the most acclaimed actors in Korea, but then threw away his career with his problematic attitudes and his degrading performances through the years.

community_snippets.snippet: [Letterboxd Review of "Marriage Story"] Okay, so the subtitles I had had a few blank spaces 🥴 So sadly I missed a little bit.However! I really enjoyed this. Loved the humour, and it's take on married life. The beginning was relatable to me. When I told folks I was getting married, I had a lot of "don't do it" vibes around me 😂It is funny how a lot of things can be relatable. We'll see how the rest of my experience goes!However, one scene was actually terrifying! However, I am aware of attitudes in the 90s and things being more 'acceptable', shall we say. A stage director and his actor wife struggle through a grueling divorce that pushes them to their personal and creative extremes. Noah Baumbach's incisive and compassionate look at a marriage breaking up and a family staying together.
